name: Dancer's calf and arch release
summary: After footwork: stretch the calf against a wall, then roll the arch under a ball, one foot at a time.
setup: Stand facing a wall, side-on to the phone. Step one foot back, heel down, and lean in until the calf stretches. Hold. Then stand on a ball under the arch and roll it slowly from heel to toe.
why: The calf stretch itself is coached elsewhere; this is the two-part cool-down and the phone just times it while you also work the arch, which it cannot see.
tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, breathe.
dosage: 2 × 45 s each side, after every footwork session.
progression: Longer holds; add the bent-knee version for the deeper calf.
regression: Shorter holds; less lean; no ball.
contraindications: Sharp calf or Achilles pain, or a painful heel first thing in the morning that has not been assessed.

faults.label: Back heel lifting
faults.tip: If the heel lifts the stretch has gone. Step the foot closer to the wall until it stays down.

faults.label: Rolling the ball too hard
faults.tip: The arch responds to slow, moderate pressure. Grinding on a hard ball can inflame it.

faults.label: Skipping the cool-down
faults.cue: Two minutes now saves a week
faults.tip: Foot and calf problems in dancers come from volume without recovery. This is the cheapest insurance there is.

faults.label: Bouncing the stretch
faults.tip: A steady hold lengthens the muscle; bouncing makes it tighten to protect itself.

guide.surface: A wall, and a tennis ball or a small roller for the arch.
guide.stop: Sharp pain in the calf or Achilles.
guide.cannotSee: The arch rolling — that part is yours to feel.

points.t: Back leg straight, heel flat, hips travelling toward the wall.
Roll slowly heel to toe with moderate pressure, about 30 s each foot.
